errors.why: gdon mi za bar means 'without doubt, certainly'; the quoted sūtra phrase is 'it will certainly come about', not a negation.

note: A faithful rendering of a commentary's section-by-section outline of the sūtra; one sūtra incipit has its sense negated.

errors.english: These arise from the consciousness produced by the two conditions of an ordinary person, and from not knowing that the sensations based on that consciousness are without a self.
errors.why: The two attachments belong to an ordinary person who does not know that both the consciousness arisen from two conditions and the feeling based on it are selfless; the consciousness is part of what is not known, not a separate source.

note: Sound rendering of the two kinds of conceit and two faults; one clause is mis-segmented, and 'manifest pride' for abhimāna is a stiff calque but intelligible.

errors.why: chāgamūtra is goat's urine (chāga = goat); the note wrongly redirects it to bovine urine.

errors.english: Smear the copper vessel to a thickness of one finger width [note: with the substance intended for preparation]. Fill the vessel halfway with fragrant water and allow the materials to float.
errors.why: Continuing from the previous side, the gold or silver jar holding the substances is sealed with a finger-thick coating and floated and boiled in a copper vessel half-filled with fragrant water; the copper vessel is not the one smeared, and it is the jar, not loose materials, that floats like a goose.

note: The eight operations of perfumery are mostly well handled, but the goose-ripening procedure is misconstrued and one ingredient is wrongly identified.
Faithful rendering of the commentary's glosses and Subhūti's questions on non-grasping and the six perfections.

errors.english: Om, I am the nature of all the Tathagatas
errors.why: tvam is 'you': the master tells the disciple 'you are the nature of all the Tathāgatas'.

fix.find: Om, I am the nature of all the Tathagatas

errors.english: The four assistant practitioners and the four commitment seals [note: term: "samaya-mudrā"] also [represent] Vairochana and the others...
errors.why: The genitive continues onto the next side ('the vases of Vairocana and the others ... take up'); the supplied '[represent]' invents a predicate the Tibetan does not have.

note: A clear and largely accurate account of the conduct vow and the wheel, conch, mirror, bow and eye-opening consecrations; the mantra's 'you' is turned into 'I'.
Accurate rendering of the prayoga, its four members, and the opponent's asiddha objection about 'not apprehended' being a property of cognition.

errors.english: The suffixes (yin) and (āyi) follow, but the letter (ī) does not.
errors.why: rjes su 'jug here is anuvṛtti: yin and āyi are carried over into the next rule, ī is not; it is a statement about the rules, not about suffixes following in a word.

errors.english: After that, by the rule "concerning (di) and (si),"
errors.why: phyis pa means 'elided': the rule is 'also when di and si have been elided', not 'after that'.

note: A competent treatment of a difficult Sanskrit grammatical commentary; a couple of metalinguistic terms are misread and some example forms are slightly mis-transcribed.

errors.english: the signs of extinction and so on appear
errors.why: zad par is kṛtsna (the kasiṇa meditation totalities), whose signs appear through meditation; it does not mean extinction.

fix.find: the signs of extinction and so on appear
fix.replace: the signs of the totalities (kṛtsna) and so on appear

note: A fluent, accurate series of illusion analogies; one meditation term is mistranslated.
Faithful rendering of the chapter close and the first signs of irreversibility in dreams.

errors.english: according to the text stating that the primary qualities are all of one nature
errors.why: The cited root line is 'the Lord (gtso bo) has the nature of all qualities', not a statement about primary qualities sharing one nature.

errors.english: This is the first section regarding the fifth topic
errors.why: lnga pa'i don du is grammatical: the first (nominative) used in the sense of the fifth (ablative) case, not a fifth topic and first section.

note: Generally sound commentary on the pīṭha list and the 36 elements; two technical remarks are misconstrued.
